source.title: Unveiling the Dynamics of Information Interplay in Supervised Learning
source.authors: Kun Song; Zhiquan Tan; Bo-Chao Zou; Hui-Min Ma; Weiran Huang

record.tranche_reason: The study trains a model on modular addition and tracks training and test accuracy over training, directly measuring the grokking behavior in V1.
record.gate_note: The grokking experiment reports training/test accuracy and MIR/HDR dynamics. The CIFAR, pruning, label-smoothing, and semi-supervised results do not test the specified grokking versions. The paper cites other grokking results, which are not recorded as findings from this study.
record.test_reason: Section 5.5 reruns Nanda et al.'s modular-addition setup (p=113, 30% train, AdamW, weight decay 1). It reports train accuracy saturating early while test accuracy starts near chance and later reaches 100%. This is a direct, if single-run, replication of V1's core effect. The study's main aim is to show off its MIR/HDR metrics, but its own accuracy curves bear on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that MIR and HDR show distinct two-stage dynamics during grokking and so can describe the phenomenon. The grokking section is one of several showcases (standard training, linear mode connectivity, label smoothing, pruning) for metrics that are also used as loss terms.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a transformer on modular addition and tracks train/test accuracy, but uses its stated single-layer ReLU architecture, p=113, 30% training fraction, and AdamW setup; it does not report a training-set-size sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: During the grokking run, MIR first rises then falls, reaching its minimum after grokking. HDR first falls, then rises, then drops sharply after grokking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matrix-information measures between representations and classifier weights show a two-phase trajectory during grokking. Their reversal precedes or accompanies the generalization jump.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024; PMLR 235)
record.problems: The grokking result is reported for one stated training-set fraction and one model configuration; the text gives no uncertainty estimates or exact epoch values for the plotted trajectory.

untested.parts: How the delay scales with training-set size: only one training fraction (30%) is used.
Not tested: no circuit or Fourier analysis, and no measure of memorizing components.
Not tested: the CIFAR experiments show no delayed generalization, and there is no initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep.
Not tested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning experiment.
Not tested: weight decay is fixed at 1 and never varied; no critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Not tested: there is no comparison of algorithms across runs.
Not tested: no optimizer or numerical-precision controls.

record.verdict_notes: The setup copies Nanda et al. (an original source), so this is a close replication with a single run and no uncertainty. It provides no evidence on delay versus dataset size or on mechanism. The CIFAR, label-smoothing, pruning and semi-supervised results are unrelated to grokking.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses one stated training-set fraction; it does not compare training-set sizes or test whether smaller training sets require more optimization.
The study does not identify or track a generalizing circuit, Fourier algorithm, memorizing components, or their removal.
No grokking-like delayed-generalization experiment on non-algorithmic data, or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep, is reported.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning experiment is reported.
Weight decay is specified for the modular-addition experiment, but the study does not test its causal role, efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The study does not compare algorithms learned across runs or architectures.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities, floating-point/softmax limits, or controls for those proposed artifacts.

rows.subject: single-layer ReLU transformer
rows.size_stated: Token encoding dimension 128; four attention heads of dimension 32; MLP hidden layer dimension 512
rows.operation_detail: Tracked MIR between data representations and the fully connected layer during modular-addition training.
rows.value: MIR initially increases, then begins to decrease as training proceeds, and reaches its lowest point after the model achieves grokking.
rows.note: This measures information interaction between representations and the classifier, not formation or removal of a mechanistically identified circuit.
rows.check: MIR between representations and classifier weights is not a circuit-formation or memorization-removal measure, so it does not bear on V2. The state relative to any version cannot be set, so 'observed' is relabelled cannot_determine.

rows.subject: single-layer ReLU transformer
rows.size_stated: Token encoding dimension 128; four attention heads of dimension 32; MLP hidden layer dimension 512
rows.operation_detail: Tracked HDR between data representations and the fully connected layer during modular-addition training.
rows.value: HDR initially decreases, then starts to increase as training proceeds, and rapidly declines from its highest point after the model achieves grokking.
rows.note: This measures information interaction between representations and the classifier, not formation or removal of a mechanistically identified circuit.
rows.check: Same as r2: HDR is an information metric, not a mechanistic progress measure. It has no version link.
